answer: A foundation model is a large AI model trained on broad, mostly unlabeled data at scale (typically via self-supervised learning) that can then be adapted — through fine-tuning, prompting, or in-context learning — to many different downstream tasks. The term was coined by Stanford's Center for Research on Foundation Models in 2021 to describe examples such as BERT, GPT-3, and DALL·E, which can span multiple modalities like text, images, and code. The key idea for your slides: instead of building a separate model per task, one general-purpose model serves as the shared "foundation," which brings big efficiency gains but also concentrates risks like bias and errors that propagate to every application built on it.
